To balance the redox reaction in acidic solution, we will follow the half-reaction method:

**Step 1: Identify the half-reactions.**

1. Oxidation half-reaction (Fe2+ to Fe3+):
   \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^- \]

2. Reduction half-reaction (MnO4- to Mn2+):
   \[ \text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \]

**Step 2: Balance the number of electrons.**

To balance the electrons transferred, we see the oxidation half-reaction produces 1 electron per Fe2+ ion, while the MnO4- reduction half-reaction requires 5 electrons. Thus, we will multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 5:

\[ 5\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 5e^- \]

**Step 3: Combine the half-reactions.**

Now we can combine the two half-reactions:

\[ \text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} \]

**Final balanced equation:**

\[ \text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \]

Final answer: MnO4- + 5Fe2+ + 8H+ -> Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O
